module_name: Preprocessing Social Data: Normalization, Deduplication, Bot Filtering, Emoji/Hashtag/Slang, Language Detection
module_description: Module 7 turns raw platform data into analysis-ready text: normalization of informal Indonesian/English, hashtag segmentation, mention/URL/emoji handling, deduplication and near-duplicate detection, language detection and code-mixing, and bot/heuristic filtering. It also teaches API-induced sampling bias (top vs recent, since/until windows) - the bias that quietly invalidates many student projects.
core_concepts: Normalization of informal and code-mixed text
learning_outcomes: C3 Clean a raw social dataset to an analysis-ready format
C4 Apply bot heuristics and quantify what was removed
C5 Identify sampling bias in an API sample and describe its consequence
methods_models: Regex-based tokenization, Unicode/emoji normalization, MinHash/LSH near-dedup, fastText/CLD language ID, classifier-based bot detection (optional)
evaluation_metrics: Preprocessing validation: leakage check (no test-time normalization differences), duplicate rate, language-ID accuracy on a gold subset
pitfalls_limitations: Over-cleaning (removing negation and sentiment-bearing tokens), silent bot over-filtering, timezone errors, drops of non-English content that reduce insight scope
tools_stack: re, unicodedata, emoji, fastText/l langid, datasketch (MinHash), pandas, clean-text or ekphrasis
commercial_platforms: Not data-driven; demo of a bot-detection heuristic (Botometer) with caveats on availability
tools_access_cost: Compute and storage costs of keeping raw + cleaned copies; free (local/library tools)
lab_activities: Cleaning pipeline with a before/after report (counts, duplicate rate, language distribution)
datasets_apis: Sample messy dataset with emojis, hashtags, code-mixed Indonesian, and duplicated replies
assessment_methods: Written analysis/design document plus a short quiz; graded on correctness of concepts and quality of justification
data_collection_workflow: Define the question -> choose platform and access route -> collect via API or permitted scrape -> archive raw with checksums -> clean and document schema -> analyse -> preserve dataset and code
textbooks: Silge and Robinson, Text Mining with R, ch. 2-4
Jurafsky & Martin, Speech and Language Processing, ch. 2
key_papers: Papers on Indonesian informal text normalization and code-mixing detection (2024-2025)
Research on API-side filters and sampling bias (2025-2026)
trends_2024_2026: 2024-2026: LLMs changed preprocessing (they tolerate noise but reward structure); datasets increasingly multimodal, so preprocessing includes OCR and transcript quality checks
industry_relevance: Core competency for social-listening analyst, insights researcher and content-strategy roles; employers (Pulsar, Talkwalker, Meltwater, Brandwatch) list sentiment/topic extraction as the default screening task for junior analysts.
localization_context: Indonesia-specific models and lexicons (IndoBERT family, NusaBERT, InSet) plus local datasets (Indonesian sentiment/emotion/hoax sets) are used as the primary lab material, because English-oriented models underperform on code-mixed colloquial Indonesian.
ethics_regulation: Annotation labor and consent, model reporting of error rates, and disclosure that automated affective labels on individuals can misrepresent them; UU PDP applies when the corpus contains identifiable user text.
case_study_scenarios: Clean a TikTok comment dump (emoji, slang, code-mixing, bots) and report what the cleaning removed.
deliverable_format: Cleaned dataset + cleaning report + reproducible notebook
